notes:
**The report no longer names services it never contacted.**

Every audit ends with a paragraph saying what left your machine. On a default
run it said five optional services were contacted and named all five —
including any that stood down before sending anything. Two commonly do: the
topic suggestions decline unless you tell Docket what your site is about, and
the deliverability check has nothing to look up when a site publishes no email
address. Neither sends a request, and the report said both did.

Connectors can now say they reached nobody, and the paragraph counts only what
was actually contacted. A service that did reach out and then failed — a quota
error from PageSpeed Insights, say — still counts, because the request was
made.

**A page in a language Docket cannot name is no longer given the wrong one.**

An airport's Irish-language section is served as `lang="en"`. Docket reported
"the text reads as Portuguese" — on a page whose own URL says `/gaeilge/`. Irish
is not one of the languages Docket can identify, so the honest answer was
silence, and the detector's own confidence score said as much: it was a hair
above the floor. Contradicting a page's declaration now needs real confidence,
measured against fourteen English pages of that same site. A genuine mismatch —
Spanish served as English, the case this check exists for — is unaffected.
